section_summary: This section documents diplomatic and commercial concerns regarding Japan's strict enforcement of navigation laws prohibiting foreign vessels from entering closed ports, fortified zones, and territorial waters in Taiwan and the Pescadores Islands. Following the detention and fining of foreign merchant ships seeking refuge from monsoons, including the Danish vessel Nicoline Maersk and Dutch tanker Juno, American shipping representatives requested U.S. government intervention. The file traces subsequent diplomatic inquiries and a sharp British protest to Tokyo, concluding with a State Department decision not to make formal representations because no American vessels had been directly penalized.

subfiles.about: Reports on an official warning from the Taiwan Government General against foreign vessels entering Mako Naval Port and details the detention and fining of the Danish steamer Nicoline Maersk.
subfiles.summary: Consul Maney transmits an official warning from the Taiwan Government General advising foreign shipping to avoid Mako Naval Port and the Pescadores Islands. He reviews the case of the Danish freighter Nicoline Maersk, which sought shelter from a monsoon near Hatto To Island, was intercepted by a Japanese warship, and whose master was held incommunicado and fined 1,000 yen under Japanese shipping regulations. The despatch notes the severe local intimidation of defense counsel in maritime cases and concludes that Japanese authorities treat the entire Pescadores archipelago as a closed naval zone.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 830/885 from American Consulate at Taihoku Regarding Navigation Warnings and the Nicoline Maersk Case

subfiles.about: Requests that American shipping lines be warned that foreign vessels are prohibited from entering Mako Naval Port and should seek storm refuge at open ports like Takao or Anping.
subfiles.summary: Kohama requests American shipping lines be warned against entering Mako Naval Port, advising storm refuge at Takao or Anping instead.
subfiles.title: Official Warning Kan Gai No. 62 from Taiwan Government General Concerning Unlawful Entry into Mako Naval Port

subfiles.about: Prohibits foreign vessels from entering closed ports or engaging in Japanese coastwise trade except under legal exceptions, distress, or ministerial permission.
subfiles.summary: Japanese statute prohibiting foreign vessels from entering closed ports except under treaty provisions, shipwreck distress, or ministerial authorization.
subfiles.title: Translation of Japanese Shipping Law Article 3 (Law No. 68 of 1905)

subfiles.about: Encloses shipping correspondence regarding Japanese navigation restrictions in Formosa and the Pescadores and suggests a formal U.S. protest on behalf of vessels seeking emergency refuge.
subfiles.summary: Duff transmits shipping correspondence and suggests protesting Japanese regulations penalizing foreign vessels seeking emergency refuge in Formosan and Pescadores waters.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin H. Duff to the Secretary of State Suggesting Protest Against Japanese Navigation Regulations

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of British consular warnings regarding Japanese authorities and closed ports in Formosa.
subfiles.summary: Plant forwards British consular warnings regarding Japanese restrictions on foreign vessels anchoring near closed ports in Formosa.
subfiles.title: Letter from Oceanic and Oriental Navigation Company Regarding Closed Ports in Formosa

subfiles.about: Transmits a report from Carter Macy Tea & Coffee Co. recounting the detentions of the Juno and a Maersk ship in the Pescadores and warning captains to avoid the area.
subfiles.summary: Transmits an agent report detailing the detentions of the Juno and a Maersk ship, urging captains to avoid the Pescadores.
subfiles.title: Letter from States Steamship Company Quoting Agent's Report on Detentions in the Pescadores

subfiles.about: Warns American shipping lines that foreign vessels are prohibited from entering Mako Naval Port and advises seeking shelter at Takao or Anping.
subfiles.summary: Copy of Taiwan Government General communication advising foreign vessels seeking refuge from monsoons to utilize Takao or Anping instead of Mako.
subfiles.title: Copy of Communication Kan Gai No. 62 Warning Against Unlawful Entry into Mako Naval Port

subfiles.about: Circulates the Taiwan Government General warning and recommends that shipping lines treat the entire Pescadores group as within the forbidden Mako naval area.
subfiles.summary: Consul Krentz warns States Steamship Company against entering Mako Naval Port, advising that restrictions cover the entire Pescadores archipelago.
subfiles.title: Consular Warning from American Consulate at Kobe to States Steamship Company

subfiles.about: Warns British shipping firms that Japanese authorities strictly enforce Article 3 of the Shipping Law, treating any unauthorized coastal anchorage outside the four open ports as an illegal entry.
subfiles.summary: Archer warns that Japanese authorities treat any anchorage outside Formosa's four open ports as illegal entry, urging strict avoidance.
subfiles.title: Confidential Circular from British Consulate at Tamsui Regarding Shipping in the Pescadores and Formosa

subfiles.about: Conveys an official request from the Taiwan Government General to distribute warnings against entering Mako Naval Port and to emphasize using only open ports for shelter.
subfiles.summary: Archer relays Taiwan Government General warnings prohibiting foreign vessels from Mako and restricting shelter to Formosa's four open ports.
subfiles.title: Letter from British Consulate at Tamsui to Carter Macy Tea & Coffee Co. Regarding Warning on Defended Ports
subfiles.to: Carter Macy Tea & Coffee Co., Inc.

subfiles.about: Informs shipping agents of the British Ambassador's concurrence on Japanese port policy, noting potential diplomatic representations and advising wireless notification in emergencies.
subfiles.summary: Archer reports the British Ambassador's concurrence, noting diplomatic protests are under consideration and advising wireless emergency communication.
subfiles.title: Letter from British Consulate at Tamsui to Carter Macy Tea & Coffee Co. on British Policy Regarding Unopened Ports
subfiles.to: Carter Macy Tea & Coffee Co., Inc.

subfiles.about: Transmits a telegram paraphrase and legal translations regarding Japanese open and closed port regulations in response to a Navy Department inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Transmits to Secretary Swanson information and translations regarding Japanese open and closed port classifications requested by the Navy Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to the Secretary of the Navy Concerning Japanese Port Regulations

subfiles.about: Explains that Japan only designates open ports for customs purposes, that closed port classifications do not exist as such, and that naval stations are closed to commercial shipping.
subfiles.from: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase explaining Japanese classification of open ports based on customs criteria, noting naval stations are closed to commercial shipping.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram from American Chargé d'Affaires at Tokyo on Japanese Port Classification

subfiles.about: Bars foreign registry vessels from entering closed ports or transporting domestic cargo and passengers, except under treaty stipulations, distress, or ministerial permission.
subfiles.summary: Translation of Article 3 of the 1899 Japanese Navigation Law barring foreign vessels from closed ports except under distress.
subfiles.title: Translation of Article 3 of the Japanese Navigation Law (Law No. 46 of March 8, 1899)

subfiles.about: Designates open ports for foreign trade throughout Japan and establishes criteria for port closure based on trade values.
subfiles.summary: Imperial ordinance enumerating designated open ports throughout Japan and establishing conditions under which ports may be closed for insufficient commerce.
subfiles.title: Translation of Imperial Ordinance Designating Open Ports (Imperial Ordinance No. 342 of July 13, 1899, as Amended)

subfiles.about: Designates Saipan, Palau, Angaur, Jaluit, and Truk as open ports in the South Seas Mandated Islands, restricting certain imports at Angaur.
subfiles.summary: Designates Saipan, Palau, Angaur, Jaluit, and Truk as open ports in the Japanese South Seas Mandated Islands.
subfiles.title: Translation of Ordinance Designating Open Ports in the South Seas Mandated Islands (Ordinance No. 13 of June 1, 1922)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Duff's suggestions concerning vessels in distress in Japanese waters and notes that the British Government is considering formal representations.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton acknowledges Duff's suggestions regarding vessels in distress and notes British consideration of formal representations to the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Edwin H. Duff Regarding Japanese Port Enforcement

subfiles.about: Encloses shipping correspondence regarding Japanese navigation restrictions and directs Ambassador Grew to ascertain discreetly what steps the British Embassy has taken.
subfiles.summary: Instructs Ambassador Grew to inquire discreetly at the British Embassy regarding any formal approach to Japan concerning navigation restrictions.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1075 from Department of State to American Ambassador at Tokyo on British Inquiries

subfiles.about: Reports that the British Embassy addressed a strong formal note to the Japanese Foreign Office in June 1936 protesting restrictions on vessels anchoring under stress of weather, and recommends similar U.S. action.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that the British lodged a formal protest regarding unopened ports, recommending similar U.S. action before incidents occur.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1974 from American Embassy Tokyo Reporting on British Representations Regarding Shipping Difficulties

subfiles.about: Encloses copies of the British diplomatic note of June 23, 1936, and the Japanese Foreign Minister's reply of August 11, 1936, regarding navigation in unopened waters.
subfiles.summary: Grew transmits copies of the British diplomatic note protesting Japanese shipping restrictions and the Japanese Government's formal reply.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1995 from American Embassy Tokyo Transmitting British and Japanese Notes on Shipping Restrictions

subfiles.about: Urges Japan to permit foreign vessels in distress to anchor in territorial waters in accordance with international practice and threatens to issue a warning Notice to Mariners.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Clive cites 1930 Hague Conference answers, demanding distress refuge in Japanese waters and warning of an impending Notice to Mariners.
subfiles.title: British Diplomatic Note No. 105 from British Ambassador to Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs Concerning Navigation Restrictions

subfiles.about: Warns shipmasters that anchoring outside open ports in Japanese territorial waters, even under stress of weather, risks arrest, heavy fines, or confiscation.
subfiles.summary: Draft notice warning shipmasters of severe penalties, including imprisonment and confiscation, for anchoring outside open ports in Japanese waters.
subfiles.title: Draft Notice to Mariners Concerning Anchorage in Japanese Territorial Waters

subfiles.about: Defends Japanese navigation regulations under Article 3 of the Navigation Law, explains restrictions in naval port sections, and cites cases of British vessels granted refuge.
subfiles.summary: Arita defends Japanese regulations, citing cases of the Christina, Minnie Moller, and Langleebrook, and explaining regulations governing naval port zones.
subfiles.title: Translation No. 165: Diplomatic Note from Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs to British Ambassador on Navigation Regulations

subfiles.about: Records that Edwin H. Duff was called in to discuss the file and directs that the file be returned to DCR.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten departmental note stating that Edwin H. Duff was called in and directing that the file be returned to DCR.
subfiles.title: Departmental File Note Regarding Return of Shipping File to DCR

subfiles.about: Analyzes the British-Japanese diplomatic notes on navigation restrictions and recommends taking no action regarding American shipping in the absence of specific incidents.
subfiles.summary: Turner analyzes the British-Japanese exchange, concluding Japan's legal position is sound, and recommends taking no action regarding American vessels.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Division of Far Eastern Affairs on British-Japanese Shipping Dispute and Policy on American Representations
